lines.text: The biggest eruption of the twentieth century was blamed on the wrong mountain.
Alaska, 1912. The column rose more than thirty kilometres, and the eruption ran for about sixty hours.
About thirteen to fifteen cubic kilometres of magma came out.
Nearby, the summit of Mount Katmai had collapsed. So Katmai was named as the vent.
It stayed that way for about forty years, until the nineteen fifties.
But the magma never came out of Katmai.
So where did it really come from? The full video has it, and it's linked right here.
